findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr175_invariant_card.py:125 computes float(f"{max_gap:.1e}") which rounds 8.215756963636522e-10 (type III, docs/generated/pr175_result_card.json:93) DOWN to 8.2e-10 (docs/generated/pr175_result_card.json:73). A field named *_ceiling must round up (8.3e-10 or 9e-10). The review-card headline 'gap <= 8e-10' is likewise below the actual max gap. findings.summary: Card field max_engine_gap_abs_ceiling (8.2e-10) understates the card's own measured maximum gap: it is computed with round-to-nearest, not a ceiling, so the shipped 'ceiling' is smaller than a value it claims to bound.

findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr175_cas_axes.py:107-134 catches only subprocess.TimeoutExpired; subprocess.run raises FileNotFoundError for an absent sage/wolframscript/lake, so the returncode==127 branch at lines 155-159 is unreachable for a missing binary (127 is a shell convention, not a Python subprocess return). wolfram/pr175_invariant_axis.wls:6 exits 3 when xAct is absent, which line 159 classifies as FAIL — a package-availability problem would be adjudicated CAS_FAIL (scientific kill) rather than CAS_BLOCKED (cas_gate.py:264 treats any FAIL as CAS_FAIL), contradicting the spec's missing_axis_outcome: CAS_BLOCKED (pr175_spec.yaml:136). Fail direction is over-strict, not silent-pass, so P2.
findings.summary: Axis runner mis-handles environment failures: a missing engine binary raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError (crash, no BLOCKED envelope), and the wls xAct-missing exit code 3 maps to FAIL -> CAS_FAIL instead of a BLOCKED status.

findings.evidence: htt/src/common/pr175_sympy_axis.py:39 computes C = structure_constants(name) and never uses it; line 43 has the vacuous disjunct 'or name in ()' (always False). sage/pr175_invariant_axis.sage:63 and wolfram/pr175_invariant_axis.wls:49-50 implement the same table-lookup n1==0. For diagonal n with a-vector (a,0,0) the constraint IS a*n1=0, but as implemented it can only fail if the frozen fixture table itself is edited — it verifies the inputs, not a computed contraction, so the obligation adds no cross-engine evidence. Either compute a_b n^{ba} from the constructed C/n objects or rename the obligation to a fixture-consistency check.
findings.summary: The class_b_vector_constraint_a_dot_n_zero obligation is a tautological fixture-table check on all four axes (n1==0 read from the input table, never computed from any constructed object), and the sympy axis carries dead/vestigial code from an abandoned stronger check.

findings.evidence: formal_pr175/Pr175Invariant/Basic.lean:45-47: hRelations checks '((0:Rat) < 1)' and '((-1:Rat) < 0)' as the sign conditions — these encode only the n2*n3 sign literals, not the correlation with the sign of h (a wrong-sign h in the fixture would still prove h_rel). The a^2=|h|*|n2 n3| part is genuinely checked (1/2^2 = 1/4*1). Contract obligation text (CAS_CONTRACT_PR175_INVARIANT.json:5) says the lean axis machine-checks 'h-relations'; what is proved is weaker. Relatedly, lean reuses the obligation key eleven_type_ricci_scalar_matches_anchor (Pr175Invariant.lean:16) for anchor-formula-vs-pinned-values arithmetic — no Ricci scalar exists on that axis — which the contract obligation text does disclose honestly, but the shared key name conflates checks of different strength across axes in the uniform envelope consumer (test_envelopes_bound_uniform_and_value_pinned).
findings.summary: Lean axis h-relation encoding is partially vacuous: the (h>0) <-> (n2*n3>0) sign biconditional from the spec is replaced by hardcoded trivially-true literals in which h never appears, and h is absent from the Rep structure entirely.

findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr175_invariant_card.py:68-81 embeds raw engine_b_gap_abs floats (e.g. 8.215756963636522e-10) into the byte-compared card; np.linalg.inv (pr175_invariant_oracle.py:164,202) goes through LAPACK whose last-ulp behavior varies with BLAS build/CPU, while runtime_identity (run_pr175_invariant_card.py:102-106) records only python/numpy/platform. The in-code comment ('a runtime change fails --check visibly') discloses the direction but the identity is insufficient to reproduce the bytes. Consider recording gaps at a stable precision (e.g. 3 significant digits) plus the exact-tolerance booleans, or add the BLAS identity.
findings.summary: Card byte-stability of the raw 17-digit float gaps depends on runtime details that runtime_identity does not record (BLAS/CPU), so --check will fail on a byte-different but scientifically identical rerun on other hardware; failure is visible/fail-closed but the disclosed identity is incomplete.

notes: No P0: the scientific content stands — all 13 gates pass live (1.22s), Engine A equals the external anchor exactly on all 11 types (anchor arithmetic independently spot-verified: III=-8, IV=-13/2, VI_h=-7/2, VII_h=-3/2, VIII=-5/2, IX=3/2 with textbook S^3/H^3 grounding), envelope timestamps are monotone in runner order confirming a single sealed --run, the adjudication carries the exact cas_gate.py cmd_adjudicate field set (tool-derived, contract-hash-bound, not hand-set), the terminal derives from adjudication bytes plus a live oracle rerun, and git_commit is the spec-pinned baseline (commit-independent). The PR-182->PR-175 runner adaptation is clean: no leftover PR-182 markers; PR175_* parse prefixes and regexes match the actual wls transcript (verified against the shipped envelope's transcript_tail, including 11 R_ keys with digits/underscores). The sympy axis importing Engine A is disclosed in the contract (its sources pin both files; obligation says 'run the exact Koszul frame chain', vs sage/wolfram 'independently re-implement'); the sage/wolfram chains are index-by-index faithful transcriptions of the same Gamma/Ricci contraction — derivation independence is carried by the external anchor, not the ports, which the contract wording tolerates. The Lean obligation text honestly discloses arithmetic-only scope. _expm is numerically ample (entrywise scale to <=0.5, 23 Taylor terms, remainder ~1e-20 with at most ~1 squaring for these O(1) ad matrices, entries provably bounded by 1 since the eps-n and a-vector terms never share a slot); the 1e-200 complex step is overflow/underflow-safe (imag*imag underflow to 0 is the desired complex-step property; smallest meaningful imag term ~1e-233 >> 1e-308), and W.T@W correctly avoids conjugation. FAIL verdict solely encodes the P1 fix-before-commit item (self-inconsistent 'ceiling' field understating its own max gap) plus P2s; none invalidates the terminal INVARIANT_ORACLE_CAS_4AXIS_PASS_ANCHOR_CONSISTENT. docs/PR_DELTAS/pr-175.md (listed in the backlog files) does not exist yet, consistent with in_progress status — expected at close.
